correctness.rationale: A selected outer vertex in petal i requires k_i >= floor(m_i/2)+1-h, where h indicates the hub; the selected hub requires sum k_i >= floor(N/2). Without the hub, any occupied petal supplies a minimal subset of exactly b_i+1 vertices. With it, global minimality forces k_i <= b_i, since otherwise the petal supplies a proper alliance. The sum of these caps is (N-q)/2 and reaches the hub threshold exactly for q <= 1, forcing saturation of every cap. Deleting any vertex other than the hub now fails the hub threshold, and any nonempty hub-free subset fails a petal threshold. This applies also to singleton petals and equal powers in the counting polynomial. For m_i=2 the two counts are r and 2^r, with missing sizes 3 through r for r>=3. The proof is unrestricted; the frozen verification and verify_alliance.py were inspected but their finite execution was not rerun. The code enumerates proper submasks until a witness is found or all have been ruled out.

originality.rationale: The two earlier findings give the full classification, parity cutoff, polynomial and friendship gap on m_i>=2. Leaves are outside their stated domain but do not yield a distinct substantial result: each singleton is an alliance, so can never occur in any other global minimum. With L leaves removed and nonleaf total N0, all nonhub thresholds are unchanged. If floor((N0+L)/2) rises above floor(N0/2), no hub minimum can survive, since its cap was at most floor(N0/2); otherwise every nonleaf alliance has unchanged feasibility. Add Lz for the leaves. If only one petal remains, the pruned graph is a clique with a single elementary size threshold; if none remain there can be no hub minimum for r>=2. This recovers the exact extension without a new mechanism.
residual_risks: The bounded comparisons do not settle first publication of the October results or rule out a separate block-graph theorem; neither limitation affects the verified overlap.
